description: The three B0 application workloads under xv6, driven through the PRODUCTION lifecycle with the workload-profile delta applied, against the accepted simulator standing in as the board-side host. This is the first execution of these workloads on any platform.

artifacts.note: the kernel is byte-identical to the accepted simulation run's; only the disk carries the three extra user programs

disk_freshness.policy: each sample gets a fresh copy of the same initial disk image
disk_freshness.detail: This run reused the disk from an earlier attempt that had already written to it, so 'disk at start' is 7aa2796553d9... rather than the pristine B0 image 6bdd8148.... The record shows it and it is not hidden: b0file creates and unlinks its own file, so the workload is self-cleaning, but the policy was still not honoured and this run therefore does not meet the sample policy on that ground alone.

frequency.caution: simulator cycles are not board time; these application results are WALL TIME on the simulator and are not a performance figure for the target

sample_policy.shortfall_note: one attempt, 2 of 3 workloads completed, and the disk was not fresh

applications.failure_reason: hit the 7200 s per-stage timeout while still progressing (cycles were advancing when the deadline fired); it did not fail, it did not finish

metrics_note: target-side cycle counts are null for application workloads, as the metrics contract requires: reading mcycle from a user program would need kernel changes made for measurement convenience. Wall time here is SIMULATOR wall time and measures the simulator, not the CPU.
